words.gloss: the Sāma, Ṛg and Yajur Vedas

hindi: साम, ऋग्, यजुर् वेद तीन, त्रयी।
english: The Sāma, Ṛg and Yajur Vedas [are] three, the triple Veda (trayī).
notes: Verbless; the copula is supplied in brackets in English only. trayī 'the triple Veda' is the name of the group of the three Vedas; the text does not say more here.

english: And the Atharvaveda and the Itihāsaveda [are] the Vedas.
notes: ca joins this sentence to the preceding one (the three Vedas); the dual dvandva has two members, Atharvaveda and Itihāsaveda. Itihāsaveda is kept as printed; the line does not say what it is. Verbless, copula bracketed in English only.

hindi: शिक्षा, कल्प, व्याकरण, निरुक्त, छन्दोविचिति, ज्योतिष — और ये अंग हैं।
english: Śikṣā (phonetics), kalpa (ritual), grammar, nirukta (etymology), the investigation of metres, jyotiṣa (astronomy) — and such are the limbs.
notes: iti closes the list of six names and is rendered as the closing label 'such are' (glossary: closing 'iti X' = Such are X), with ca 'and' joining it to the preceding sentence; the construction is loose, so the translation stays literal. The six names are kept with short literal glosses; the precise sense of each (e.g. chandas-viciti, kalpa) is not argued here. aṅga is 'limb' (of the Vedas is understood, not stated).
lines_deva: शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो.विचितिर् ज्योतिषम् इति च-अङ्गानि
lines_iast: śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando.vicitir jyotiṣam iti ca-aṅgāni

words.gloss: from the establishing of own dharma

hindi: यह त्रयी-धर्म चार वर्णों के और आश्रमों के अपने धर्म की स्थापना से उपकारी।
english: This dharma of the triple Veda (trayī-dharma) [is] beneficial, through the establishing of [their] own dharma of the four varṇas and of the āśramas.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. 'caturṇām' agrees with varṇānām; whether it also covers āśramāṇām is not stated (the āśramas are commonly four, but the line does not say). sva-dharma is taken as 'own dharma' of each, '[their]' is supplied in brackets. aupakārika = 'helpful, beneficial' (from upakāra).
lines_deva: एष त्रयी.धर्मश् चतुर्णां वर्णानाम् आश्रमाणां च स्व.धर्म.स्थापनाद् औपकारिकः
lines_iast: eṣa trayī.dharmaś caturṇāṃ varṇānām āśramāṇāṃ ca sva.dharma.sthāpanād aupakārikaḥ

hindi: ब्राह्मण का अपना धर्म अध्ययन, अध्यापन, यजन, याजन, दान, प्रतिग्रह।
english: The own dharma of the brāhmaṇa [is] study, teaching, sacrificing, causing [others] to sacrifice, giving and receiving.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. yājana is the causative-derived noun beside yajana; 'causing [others] to sacrifice' is the literal rendering, 'officiating' is the usual sense. pratigraha = receiving (what is received is not stated). sva-dharma is printed without a compound dot (svadharmo) here and in units 14 and 16 but with dots in unit 4; read as a plain compound, no flag.
lines_deva: स्वधर्मो ब्राह्मणस्य अध्ययनम् अध्यापनं यजनं याजनं दानं प्रतिग्रहश् च
lines_iast: svadharmo brāhmaṇasya adhyayanam adhyāpanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ dānaṃ pratigrahaś ca

hindi: क्षत्रिय का अध्ययन, यजन, दान, शस्त्र से जीविका, प्राणियों की रक्षा।
english: Of the kṣatriya [are] study, sacrificing, giving, livelihood by weapons and protection of beings.
notes: Verbless; 'own dharma' (svadharma) is understood from unit 5 but not supplied. The '-' join 'kṣatriyasya-adhyayanaṃ' is two words. bhūta = being(s), creatures.
lines_deva: क्षत्रियस्य-अध्ययनं यजनं दानं शस्त्र.आजीवो भूत.रक्षणं च
lines_iast: kṣatriyasya-adhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ dānaṃ śastra.ājīvo bhūta.rakṣaṇaṃ ca

hindi: वैश्य का अध्ययन, यजन, दान, कृषि और पशुपालन, वाणिज्य।
english: Of the vaiśya [are] study, sacrificing, giving, agriculture and cattle-keeping, and trade.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. kṛṣi-pāśupālye is a dual dvandva (two members, 'and'); the final ca adds vaṇijyā.
lines_deva: वैश्यस्य-अध्ययनं यजनं दानं कृषि.पाशुपाल्ये वणिज्या च
lines_iast: vaiśyasya-adhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ dānaṃ kṛṣi.pāśupālye vaṇijyā ca

hindi: शूद्र का द्विजातियों की शुश्रूषा, वार्ता, कारु और कुशीलव का कर्म।
english: Of the śūdra [are] service of the twice-born, economic activity (vārttā), and the works of artisans and kuśīlavas.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. śuśrūṣā: glossary 3.3 has 'obedience' for the wife's duty; here, for the śūdra's duty toward the twice-born, 'service' is kept (Book 1 decision, glossary line 1.3); Hindi keeps शुश्रूषा. kuśīlava kept untranslated (glossary); karma = works (the works of artisans and kuśīlavas). kāru = artisan (glossary).

words.gloss: worship of gods, fathers and guests

hindi: गृहस्थ का अपने धर्म से जीविका, तुल्यों के साथ, असमान ऋषियों वालों के साथ विवाह, ऋतु में गमन, देव, पितृ, अतिथि की पूजा, भृत्यों के प्रति त्याग, शेष भोजन।
english: Of the householder [are] livelihood by own dharma; marriage with equals, with [those] of different sages; going in the season; worship of gods, fathers and guests; giving to servants; and eating the remainder.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. tulyaiḥ and asamāna-ṛṣibhiḥ are two instrumentals with no ca between them, so they are not joined (the sense 'with equals who have different sages' is possible but not stated). asamāna-ṛṣi = not having the same sage(s), literal; the lineage sense (gotra/pravara) is not imported. ṛtu-gāmitva = 'going in the season' (literal); what season and whom is not stated. tyāga with locative bhṛtyeṣu: literal 'giving up / giving among servants'; 'liberality' is a possible sense; bhṛtya = servant/dependant. pitṛ = fathers (ancestors possible). Hindi list takes commas only (glossary 1.2), the final ca is carried by the comma.
lines_deva: गृहस्थस्य स्वधर्म.आजीवस् तुल्यैर् असमान.ऋषिभिर् वैवाह्यम् ऋतु.गामित्वं देव.पित्र्.अतिथि.पूजा भृत्येषु त्यागः शेष.भोजनं च
lines_iast: gṛhasthasya svadharma.ājīvas tulyair asamāna.ṛṣibhir vaivāhyam ṛtu.gāmitvaṃ deva.pitr.atithi.pūjā bhṛtyeṣu tyāgaḥ śeṣa.bhojanaṃ ca

words.gloss: lasting to the end of life

hindi: ब्रह्मचारी का स्वाध्याय, अग्निकार्य और अभिषेक, भिक्षा-व्रतित्व, आचार्य के पास प्राणान्त तक की वृत्ति, उसके अभाव में गुरु-पुत्र के पास या सहब्रह्मचारी के पास।
english: Of the brahmacārin [are] self-study (svādhyāya), fire-rite and ablution, the state of keeping the alms-vow, a way of life lasting to the end of life with the teacher, in the absence of that [teacher] with the preceptor's son, or with a fellow-brahmacārin.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. agni-kārya is literally 'the task of fire' (fire-rite); abhiṣeka = ablution/sprinkling. bhaikṣa-vratitva = state of having begging (alms) as vow. vṛtti: way of life / livelihood / conduct, medium confidence; prāṇa-antikī is a feminine bahuvrīhi 'having the end of life as its end'. The locatives ācārye, guru-putre, sa-brahmacāriṇi are rendered 'with'; 'in' (the case of) is the bare sense. The edition prints 'sa-brahma.cāriṇi' with a hyphen and a dot; taken as one compound (sa- 'together with'), no flag. guru = preceptor, ācārya = teacher.
lines_deva: ब्रह्म.चारिणः स्वाध्यायो अग्नि.कार्य.अभिषेकौ भैक्ष.व्रतित्वम् आचार्ये प्राण.अन्तिकी वृत्तिस् तद्.अभावे गुरु.पुत्रे स-ब्रह्म.चारिणि वा
lines_iast: brahma.cāriṇaḥ svādhyāyo agni.kārya.abhiṣekau bhaikṣa.vratitvam ācārye prāṇa.antikī vṛttis tad.abhāve guru.putre sa-brahma.cāriṇi vā

words.gloss: wearing of matted hair and hide
worship of deities, fathers and guests

hindi: वानप्रस्थ का ब्रह्मचर्य, भूमि पर शय्या, जटा और अजिन का धारण, अग्निहोत्र और अभिषेक, देवता, पितृ, अतिथि की पूजा, वन्य आहार।
english: Of the vānaprastha [are] brahmacarya, a bed on the ground, wearing of matted hair and hide, agni-hotra and ablution, worship of deities, fathers and guests, and forest food.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. brahmacarya is kept as a term (celibacy / the student's way of life are possible senses). bhūmau śayyā literally 'a bed on the ground'. jaṭā = matted locks; ajina = (animal) hide. agni-hotra kept as a term. vanya = belonging to the forest; the sense 'wild food' is not stated.
lines_deva: वानप्रस्थस्य ब्रह्मचर्यं भूमौ शय्या जटा.अजिन.धारणम् अग्नि.होत्र.अभिषेकौ देवता.पित्र्.अतिथि.पूजा वन्यश् च-आहारः
lines_iast: vānaprasthasya brahmacaryaṃ bhūmau śayyā jaṭā.ajina.dhāraṇam agni.hotra.abhiṣekau devatā.pitr.atithi.pūjā vanyaś ca-āhāraḥ

words.gloss: state of having conquered the senses

hindi: परिव्राजक की जितेन्द्रियता, अनारम्भ, निष्किंचनता, संग का त्याग, भिक्षा-व्रत, अनेक स्थानों पर और वन में निवास, बाह्य और आभ्यन्तर शुचिता।
english: Of the parivrājaka [are] mastery of the senses, non-undertaking, possessing nothing, giving up of attachment, the alms-vow, dwelling in many places and in the forest, and external and internal purity.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. anārambha = non-undertaking (of works), literal. anekatra = in more than one place (many places). The final ca joins the whole last item; bāhya-ābhyantara is a two-member dvandva ('external and internal'). The word 'bhaikṣavrata' is printed without a dot; 'bhaikṣa-vratitva' of unit 10 is similar. śauca = purity (Hindi शुचिता) per the glossary.
lines_deva: परिव्राजकस्य जित.इन्द्रियत्वम् अनारम्भो निष्किञ्चनत्वं सङ्ग.त्यागो भैक्षव्रतम् अनेकत्र-अरण्ये च वासो बाह्य.आभ्यन्तरं च शौचम्
lines_iast: parivrājakasya jita.indriyatvam anārambho niṣkiñcanatvaṃ saṅga.tyāgo bhaikṣavratam anekatra-araṇye ca vāso bāhya.ābhyantaraṃ ca śaucam

hindi: सभी के अहिंसा, सत्य, शुचिता, असूया का अभाव, करुणा, क्षमा।
english: Of all [are] non-injury, truth, purity, absence of envy, compassion and forbearance.

text_flags.why: possible: final ā shortened (anasūyā + ānṛśaṃsyam); the stem anasūya is not an attested noun here

notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English, none in Hindi. The printed 'anasūya' (Devanagari अनसूय) before ānṛśaṃsyam is read anasūyā (f., 'absence of envy / fault-finding'); the short final -a is a possible slip for -ā (anasūyā + ānṛśaṃsyam, which would sandhi to anasūyānṛśaṃsyam), so flagged as possible. anṛśaṃsya = compassion (glossary). 'sarveṣām' presumably refers to all the classes just listed; not supplied.
lines_deva: सर्वेषाम् अहिंसा सत्यं शौचम् अनसूय आनृशंस्यं क्षमा च
lines_iast: sarveṣām ahiṃsā satyaṃ śaucam anasūya ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā ca

hindi: अपना धर्म स्वर्ग के लिए और अनन्तता के लिए।
english: Own dharma [is] for heaven and for endlessness.
notes: Verbless; copula bracketed in English. ānantya = endlessness / infinity (some read 'eternal bliss'; the line does not say). The text gives dative purpose; the verb is not supplied beyond the bracketed copula.

hindi: उसका अतिक्रमण होने पर लोक संकर से उच्छिन्न हो जाए।
english: In transgression of that, the world would be uprooted through confusion (saṅkara).
notes: tasya refers to the svadharma of unit 14. saṅkara = confusion, mixing (of the classes is the usual sense but is not stated here). ucchidyeta is the optative passive of ud-√chid; 'uprooted' follows the glossary for the ucch- forms, 'cut off / destroyed' is possible.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. sam-√dhā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: इसलिए राजा प्राणियों के अपने धर्म को विचलित न कराए। क्योंकि अपने धर्म का संधान करता हुआ मरने के बाद और यहाँ आनन्दित होता है।
english: Therefore the king should not cause the own dharma of beings to swerve. For, joining [his] own dharma, [he] rejoices both after death and here.
notes: vyabhicārayet is a causative of vi-abhi-√car ('go astray'); 'cause to swerve' is literal, 'let [beings] deviate from' is the sense of the construction. sandadhāna (sam-√dhā, middle participle): 'joining, putting together'; 'holding to / adhering to' is a possible sense, medium confidence. The subject of nandati is not stated; '[he]' is bracketed. pretya = having departed, 'after death'. 'ca … ca' is 'both … and'; Hindi has one और. bhūtānām: of beings (creatures), as in unit 6.
lines_deva: तस्मात् स्वधर्मं भूतानां राजा न व्यभिचारयेत्
स्वधर्मं सन्दधानो हि प्रेत्य च-इह च नन्दति
lines_iast: tasmāt svadharmaṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā na vyabhicārayet
svadharmaṃ sandadhāno hi pretya ca-iha ca nandati

words.gloss: with the position of varṇas and āśramas made

hindi: व्यवस्थित आर्य-मर्यादा वाला, की गई वर्ण-आश्रम-स्थिति वाला, त्रयी से रक्षित लोक प्रसन्न होता है, डूबता नहीं।
english: The world, with the ārya boundary established, with the position of varṇas and āśramas made, protected by the triple Veda, becomes serene, does not sink.
notes: Both first-line compounds are bahuvrīhi adjectives of lokaḥ. maryādā = boundary, limit; sthiti = standing, position (order). prasīdati: 'becomes clear/serene/gracious'; sīdati: 'sinks, languishes'; medium-high confidence. trayī = the triple Veda as in unit 1. The two clauses have no connecting word and are kept asyndetic.
